customer_john: Hey team — after you enabled the new quant calibration last night (int8_auto_calib_v3) our /v1/generate p99 jumped from ~800ms to ~2.6s in eu-west-1. This started ~23:40 UTC. Example request id: req_89ab34fc. Can you escalate? :frowning:

emily_support: Sorry about that — thanks for flagging. Can you share the exact model and a minimal request body that reproduces? We'll escalate to SRE/ML. :pray:

customer_john: Model: redwood/gpt-large-v2, profile: int8_auto_calib_v3, tenant: t-cust-123. Minimal curl I used:

```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-large-v2","input":"Summarize: The quarterly revenue...","max_tokens":128}'
```

emily_support: I pulled a sample and ran locally against the same profile — p99 ~2.4s for batch=1. Noting cache hit rate for this tenant is ~0 (cache TTL=0). Paging @ravi_sre and @julia_ml to look at quant calibration impact. :eyes:

ravi_sre: Looking at runtime traces for that tenant and profile. Observations: token-level latency spike matches increased time in dequant/scale ops. I see repeated memcpy calls in the timeline. Quick log excerpt:

```
[2026-03-16T23:42:12Z] req=req_89ab34fc model=gpt-large-v2 profile=int8_auto_calib_v3 step=attn_kv_fetch time_ms=12
[2026-03-16T23:42:12Z] req=req_89ab34fc step=quant_dequant_copy time_ms=780
[2026-03-16T23:42:12Z] req=req_89ab34fc step=kernel_dispatch time_ms=40
[2026-03-16T23:42:13Z] req=req_89ab34fc total_token_time_ms=820
```

It looks like the new calibration inserts a per-token scaling memcpy on the hot path. Need ML to confirm intent.

julia_ml: Confirming — int8_auto_calib_v3 added a per-shard compensation stage to reduce accuracy drift across long prefixes. It introduces an extra per-token scale memcpy to apply noise-compensation factors. In our perf lab this added ~50–120ms p99, not ~1.6s, so something else is amplifying it (likely cache misses or kernel mismatch). Two hypotheses: (1) tenant cache TTL=0 causing repeated KV recompute; (2) kernel selector falling back to slower code path because sequence length distribution shifted.

emily_support: Customer uses dedicated pool in eu-west-1 and we enabled v3 as canary last night for that pool. Their config disables prefix caching. So hypothesis 1 is plausible.

ravi_sre: I ran a repro against the tenant with tracing and perf counters. Repro steps I used:

```
# reproduce
TOKEN=xxxxx
while true; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/gpt-large-v2","input":"Summarize: The quarterly revenue...","max_tokens":128}' > /dev/null
  sleep 0.5
done

# perf snapshot (sample)
quant_dequant_copy: 740ms (p99)
kernel_dispatch_fp16: 35ms (median)
kv_recompute: 120ms (per request)
```

When I temporarily enabled prefix caching for the tenant, p99 dropped to ~400ms (still a bit higher than baseline).

julia_ml: Mitigation options ranked: 
1) toggle the profile to a conservative int8 variant (int8_safe_fallback) that removes the extra memcpy and uses a slightly looser calibration;
2) rollback to int8_auto_calib_v2;
3) enable prefix caching for affected tenants;
4) short-term, allow automatic fallback to fp16 for this tenant's model when per-token dequant exceeds threshold.

emily_support: I recommend (1) + (3) as fastest: flip tenant to int8_safe_fallback and enable prefix caching TTL=30s. @ops-bot can you open a rollback/change job? We'll coordinate smoke tests.

ops-bot: Change request created: CR-3456 — move t-cust-123 from int8_auto_calib_v3 -> int8_safe_fallback and set prefix_cache_ttl=30s on pool eu-west-1. Scheduled for immediate rollout (5m window). Assigned: ravi_sre, julia_ml. :robot_face:

ravi_sre: Applying change now, running smoke and perf checks.

[5m later]
ravi_sre: Rolled profile and enabled cache. New metrics for tenant t-cust-123: p95=210ms, p99=380ms. Perf traces show quant_dequant_copy now ~45ms (p99). Customer visible latency improved. :thumbsup:

customer_john: Confirmed — latency back to expected range. Thanks everyone, appreciate the quick turnaround.

emily_support: Closing loop: action items — (a) add perf guard to calibration ci (block deploy if p99 increase >25% on step-level); (b) add canary alert for calibration rollouts that checks p95/p99 for a small set of tenants; (c) document rollback runbook for quant profile toggles. Owners: julia_ml, ravi_sre, emily_support. ETA 48h.

julia_ml: I'll open RFC for calibration changes and include perf tests. ravi_sre — please add a playbook snippet for prefix-cache quick-enable.

emily_support: Thanks team — marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
